# SPD-077 — A pr-landing ticket whose pull request merges after its session stopped stays active

## Brief
Eric (2026-09-15): BAD-058 showed as active after its work had landed. The session that ran it opened PR https://github.com/0snug0/BadTakes/pull/361, recorded the outcome "PR … opened (ready)" (event 3305, 13:13:56), and stopped. The PR squash-merged later (e4bf836 on main), but no session was left to run `ticket move --status done`, delete the worktree and its local branch, or commit the ledger. A later session found it only because Eric asked, and closed it out by hand at 13:57.

The gap: under `landing: pr` a ticket's done move depends on the landing session still being alive when the pull request merges. Nothing records that a ticket is waiting on a pull request, and nothing notices when that pull request has merged or closed.

Make a merged or closed pull request reach the ledger without relying on the session that opened it. The approach is the implementer's to propose; options include recording the PR against the ticket when it is opened and reconciling at board time or SessionStart (`gh pr view <branch> --json state`, the one read the classifier allows), a Stop hold on a session that leaves an open PR on an active ticket, or a scheduled reconcile. Whatever reconciles must not merge anything, and must never act on a PR the ledger did not record.

Done when: a ticket whose recorded PR has merged is surfaced on the board (or moved to done with the PR URL in its Outcome) with no action from the session that opened it; a closed-unmerged PR is surfaced, not moved; the landed worktree and local branch cleanup is either done or named as owed; covered by tests; CLAUDE.md's In another project § Landing updated to match.

## Size, persona and model decision
Queued; size when picked up. Likely one engineer on opus: bin/spud and its hooks, with tests. An architect pass first only if the fix changes what the Stop hook holds.
